officialDocs.label: API plans, user cap and app review

verdict.summary: Creating a Public API app is self-serve and free, but the Start for Free plan caps you at 10 connected users until Withings reviews the app (a 10-question form), and unlimited users or AI model-training rights need a paid Enterprise or Advanced Biomarkers contract. Since October 12, 2026, Withings accounts created after that date need an active Withings+ membership to share data with free-plan apps.

evidence.label: inferred

timeToProd.assumes: Staying on the free plan and passing Withings' app review to lift the 10-user cap. Unlimited users or no Withings+ requirement means negotiating Enterprise, which takes longer.

verdict.cost: Start for Free plan has no fee. Enterprise and Advanced Biomarkers are custom-priced by active users. End users with Withings accounts created after October 12, 2026 need Withings+ on the free plan.

steps.title: Create a Public API app
steps.detail: Sign in to the developer dashboard, choose a Public API integration, enter name, description and registered callback URL, then copy the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The application type label comes from a third-party guide.

steps.title: Expose a public HTTPS callback
steps.detail: Deploy the callback or use an HTTPS tunnel for local development; keep it on port 443 and under 255 characters.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Callback constraints come from a third-party guide.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://account.withings.com/oauth2_user/authorize2 with comma-separated scopes and state. Exchange the code within 30 seconds by POSTing action=requesttoken to https://wbsapi.withings.net/v2/oauth2.

steps.title: Test with demo mode
steps.detail: Add &mode=demo to the authorize URL to get a demo account's data without a device.

steps.title: Subscribe to notifications
steps.detail: Subscribe per user per appli, receive the POST webhook, then pull with lastupdate. Don't poll more than once every 10 minutes per user.

steps.title: Draft the review answers and privacy policy
steps.detail: Describe the product, the biomarkers requested and how data is protected; prepare the demo link.

steps.title: Submit the app review form
steps.detail: Ten questions, about 5 minutes; needs client ID, live app or demo link and privacy policy URL.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The link redirects to www.withings.com/en-us/pages/withings-api-plans-form, which returned 403 to our non-browser client.

steps.title: Withings review
steps.detail: Withings raises your user cap to fit your use case once approved.

steps.title: Consider Enterprise for scale or AI training
steps.detail: Contact Withings if you need unlimited users, higher rate limits, HIPAA, removal of the Withings+ requirement, or AI model training rights.

blockers.symptom: New users can't connect once 10 accounts are linked
blockers.cause: Start for Free apps are capped at 10 active users until Withings reviews the app.
blockers.fix: Submit the app review form, or move to Enterprise. Disconnected users free their slot.

blockers.symptom: A newly signed-up Withings user connects but no data is shared
blockers.cause: Accounts created after October 12, 2026 need an active Withings+ membership for free-plan apps; sharing pauses if it lapses.
blockers.fix: Ask the user to subscribe to Withings+, or get the requirement lifted under an Enterprise agreement.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact API response in this case isn't documented.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an invalid-code error (status 304 in the body)
blockers.cause: Authorization codes expire after 30 seconds, or the request omitted action=requesttoken.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately server-side and include action=requesttoken.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 200 responses that contain {"status":601} or other non-zero status
blockers.cause: Withings returns errors in the JSON body; 601 means the per-app rate limit (120 req/min on the free plan per a third-party guide) was hit.
blockers.fix: Check body.status, back off, and switch from polling to notifications.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: POST to wbsapi.withings.net/v2/oauth2 with only action=requesttoken returned HTTP 200 with {"status":503,"error":"Invalid Params: Missing params"}. The 120 req/min figure is unverified.

blockers.symptom: Users get logged out after a token refresh
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens rotate; the previous one becomes invalid 8 hours after a new one is issued.
blockers.fix: Persist the new refresh token from every refresh response.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 3 hours, refresh tokens 1 year, authorization codes 30 seconds.
AI model training rights appear only in the Advanced Biomarkers plan's 'AI model training contract', so training models on Withings data from a free or Enterprise app isn't covered.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Our reading of the plan comparison table; we didn't find a clause in the API terms.

nuances.text: The Withings+ requirement also covers data shared through Apple Health or Google Health, so routing around it isn't possible.
An 'active user' is a connected account with valid authorization; disconnecting frees the slot.
Cellular, RPM and OnSite solutions are separate contract-only products with their own flows.
